title: Huang Renxun and Hinton's War of Words: The AI Extinction Probability Debate Reflects Deep Industry Divisions
key_facts: Huang assigned a 0% probability to AI causing human extinction (CBS interview)
Anthropic's Evan Hubinger wrote on X the chance of extinction within ten years is over 10%
Huang named Geoffrey Hinton, who has put the risk at 10 to 20% within thirty years, on a New York Times podcast
Researcher Jacob Coxon criticised AI firms on leaving Anthropic and OpenAI
Amodei wrote in September that AI building the next AI has sped up development; Altman and Musk agreed
BigGo says both numbers are belief, not measurement; the BBC found many insiders doubt extinction scenarios
quote_evidence: Jensen Huang publicly assigned a probability of zero to AI causing human extinction, while just days earlier, Anthropic's alignment science lead Evan Hubinger had offered a starkly different assessment.
Skeptics point out that the probabilities claimed by pessimists are not the result of measurement, but expressions of belief.
why_it_matters_hint: The gap between zero and ten percent shows the argument is about beliefs, not data.
notes: Full text read. It is an opinion-style analysis; it also retells a July OpenAI-Hugging Face incident (about 1,200 agents) and cites the BBC; those details were not independently checked. Reply link: BigGo ties Huang's CBS/NYT remarks to Hubinger and Hinton; we say 'read as'. Score lowered 6 to 5.
